title: A Locker for the Prom
premise: Jude Villalobos, a senior coder who runs an anonymous exposé account about Ridgemont High, starts receiving handwritten notes from the school's legendary ghost — notes that name her, predict events, and are written in ink that shouldn't exist. The ghost turns out to be the digital afterimage of a student who died in 1998, whose death was covered up by the school board to protect a booster-funded football dynasty. As Jude investigates, she must choose between protecting her scholarship-bound best friend Marcus — whose father sits on the board — and publishing the truth before the final game of the season, when the board plans to quietly seal the archived records forever. In the end Jude exposes the cover-up at the homecoming-adjacent championship game, the board resigns, and the ghost's notes stop arriving, leaving one last message: 'You were never alone.'
about_author: Jude Halloran is a former high school debate coach from the Pacific Northwest who writes stories about teenagers who refuse to look away. This is their second novel inspired by a real small-town scandal they watched unfold from the faculty lounge.

chapters.title: Ninety-One Days
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Opening on her countdown app and her anonymous account @ridgemontleaks, we see her cynical, watchful world: code, cafeteria politics, and a school that worships its football team. She posts a small story about a janitor being fired unfairly. Emotional beat: restless dissatisfaction disguised as detachment.

chapters.title: The First Note
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A folded note appears inside her locked locker: 'You count days like a prisoner. So did I.' The handwriting is old-fashioned; the ink shimmers faintly blue under her phone flashlight. No camera in the hallway caught anyone approaching. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: Marcus Knows Nothing
chapters.summary: Dual POV, mostly Marcus. Her best friend notices Jude jumping at shadows; his father, board member Dale Okafor, warns him to keep clear of 'that leak account.' We feel Marcus's loyalty straining between family and Jude. Emotional beat: warmth undercut by the first hairline crack of divided allegiance.

chapters.title: Ink That Isn't Ink
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She runs chemical tests on the note in chemistry class — the pigment matches nothing in any database, and it's cold to the touch. A second note arrives naming her anonymous handle, which no living person knows. Emotional beat: fear converting into obsession.

chapters.title: The Girl From 1998
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with librarian Ms. Ferro as reluctant ally. Yearbooks reveal Dana Whitlock, a coding prodigy who drowned in the pool the night of the 1998 championship — ruled an accident, memorial quietly removed. Emotional beat: grief for a girl erased, and the first taste of a buried pattern.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. He finds his father shredding-era boxes in the district office basement and pockets a 1998 memo referencing 'the Whitlock settlement.' He tells Jude nothing. Emotional beat: complicity beginning; guilt he can't name yet.

chapters.title: Notes in Impossible Places
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Notes appear inside her closed laptop, in a printed email, in wet cement outside the gym — always signed 'D,' always knowing what she'll do next. She sets a trap with motion sensors; the sensors record nothing but the notes still come. Emotional beat: terror braided with the thrill of being truly seen.

chapters.title: Homecoming Is a Lie
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At homecoming, the school unveils a glossy 'Tradition of Excellence' exhibit scrubbing 1998 entirely. Jude watches Principal Reyes flinch when Dana's photo nearly surfaces. Emotional beat: public pageantry as machinery of forgetting; Jude's anger crystallizes into purpose.

chapters.title: The Account Gets a Follower
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Someone starts replying to @ridgemontleaks with corrections only an insider could know — steering her toward booster club finances. Meanwhile the district offers her a 'STEM leadership scholarship' she never applied for. Emotional beat: the seduction of power, and recognizing a bribe when it wears a bow.

chapters.title: Dana's Drive
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, technical chapters within chapters. Following the ghost's clues, Jude recovers a corrupted 1998 hard drive from the pool equipment room and begins reconstructing files: training logs, injury reports, and a draft article Dana never published. Emotional beat: communion across time; two coders, twenty-five years apart, working the same problem.

chapters.title: The Night of the Accident
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Dana (in recovered journal entries) and Jude reading them. Dana's entries reveal she discovered players were being dosed with performance drugs sanctioned by the boosters, and that she planned to publish before the championship. Emotional beat: dread mounting as history walks toward its fixed point.

chapters.title: Marcus Breaks
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. His father discovers the stolen memo; the confrontation at home turns physical-then-silent. Dale reveals he was a player on the '98 team and has spent his life paying for his silence. Emotional beat: Marcus realizing loyalty to family and loyalty to truth have become opposites.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Principal Reyes and Dale Okafor jointly offer Jude a full ride to any state school and a guaranteed internship — if she hands over the drive and shuts down the account. They mention her mother's precarious job at the district. Emotional beat: power showing its polite face; duty versus survival made concrete.

chapters.title: Ghost Logic
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She finally asks the notes directly: what do you want? The reply: 'Not revenge. Publication. Finish my article.' Jude realizes Dana doesn't want justice for herself — she wants the story completed, bylined by someone alive. Emotional beat: the ghost reframed from haunting to mentorship.

chapters.title: Source Code
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Decryption finishes: the drive contains drug procurement records, a booster slush fund, and audio of Coach Brandt threatening Dana hours before her death. Jude builds a dead-man's-switch publication system so the truth releases even if she's stopped. Emotional beat: quiet competence as courage; the coder becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: Someone Deletes Everything
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, panicked pacing. A district IT contractor wipes the archive servers and the library's microfilm room floods 'accidentally.' The dead-man's-switch holds, but Jude knows they've escalated — next will be her. Emotional beat: isolation and vertigo; the machine protecting itself.

chapters.title: The Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. He confronts his father with everything and records Dale's tearful admission about the '98 cover-up — then must decide whether giving it to Jude is betrayal or the only loyalty left. He chooses Jude. Emotional beat: love expressed as truth-telling; the friendship reforged at higher stakes.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Championship night: forty thousand fans, live stream, the board assembled in the box seats. Jude has until halftime to decide whether to trigger the release. Notes from Dana arrive one final time: 'Whenever you're ready. I waited twenty-five years; you don't have to wait another minute.' Emotional beat: held breath; the whole book converging on a single click.

chapters.title: Halftime
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She triggers the release mid-halftime show: documents, audio, and Dana's finished article cascade onto every screen in the stadium and every feed online. The crowd's roar curdles into chaos as the jumbotron displays the headline. Emotional beat: catharsis — the sentence she'd been serving ends not at graduation but here.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unscripted
chapters.summary: Rotating POV among Jude, Marcus, and Ms. Ferro over the following week. Board members resign, Coach Brandt is arrested, the scholarship offer evaporates — and Jude discovers she no longer wants the version of the future she was bribed with. Emotional beat: disorientation of victory; the cost tallied honestly.

chapters.title: A Locker for Dana
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The school dedicates a memorial locker to Dana Whitlock; Jude places the original notes inside, now ordinary ink on ordinary paper. The impossible blue is gone. She publishes Dana's article under both their names. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into legacy; letting go.

chapters.title: Day Zero
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, final chapter. Graduation day. Her countdown app hits zero and she deletes it. A last note waits in her cap's lining — not from Dana, but in her own handwriting, time-slipped: 'Tell them anyway.' She smiles, walks the stage, and starts writing what comes next. Emotional beat: release, agency, and the open door of an unwritten future.
